hook.text: Ten servers run your app. One gets all the traffic while nine sit idle. A load balancer fixes that.

buildup.text: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple servers so no single one is overwhelmed.

discovery.text: Algorithms vary: round-robin, least connections, or weighted. Each has trade-offs for different workloads.

twist.text: Load balancers also detect unhealthy servers and stop sending traffic to them. Failed nodes are silently bypassed.

climax.text: Cloud load balancers like AWS ALB and GCP Load Balancing handle millions of requests per second automatically.

punchline.text: Spread the load. No single server should carry everything.

quiz.question: What additional function do load balancers serve beyond distributing traffic?
options: They detect unhealthy servers and stop routing traffic to them
They encrypt all stored data on backend servers
They automatically write code for new microservices

details.summary: Load balancers distribute incoming traffic across multiple servers to prevent any single server from becoming overwhelmed. They improve availability by routing around failed instances and enable horizontal scaling by adding more servers behind the balancer.
details.whyItMatters: Without load balancing, a single server failure takes down the entire application. Load balancers are the most fundamental building block for high availability in the cloud.
takeaways: Traffic is distributed across multiple healthy servers
Failed instances are detected and removed from rotation
Enables horizontal scaling by adding more backend servers

faq.question: What algorithms do load balancers use?
faq.answer: Common algorithms include round-robin, least connections, weighted round-robin, and IP hash. Layer 7 load balancers can route based on URL path, headers, or cookies. The best choice depends on whether sessions are sticky and how even the workload is.

faq.question: What is the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing?
faq.answer: Layer 4 balancers route based on IP address and TCP port without inspecting content. Layer 7 balancers inspect HTTP headers, URLs, and cookies for smarter routing. L7 is more flexible but adds latency due to deeper packet inspection.
